verdict: Ads are running and converting, but lead tracking is broken right now.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, Google Ads recorded 10 conversions on $956.48 in spend — but a disconnect between the ad platform and your lead system means those conversions are not showing up as leads in your pipeline, so your reported lead count reads zero. This is a tracking problem, not a demand problem. Separately, ad spend was uneven across the period, with 7 days of zero spend and a weekly average of roughly $15 per day, which points to a budget cap or billing interruption rather than an intentional pause. Conversion tracking is being repaired so the full picture becomes visible, and your Local Services Ads are scheduled to re-enable September 1st as heating season ramps up. Once attribution is restored and LSA is live, you should see lead counts and cost-per-lead reporting accurately again.

highlights.phrase: conversions recorded by Google Ads in the last 28 days, currently invisible to your pipeline due to a tracking gap being fixed
opportunities marked won in your CRM over the last 28 days, showing real pipeline activity despite the reporting disconnect
actions taken on your Google Business Profile this period — calls, direction requests, and website clicks from organic searchers

watch_item.issue: A disconnect between Google Ads and your lead system is causing 10 recorded conversions to go uncounted, making lead volume appear as zero this period.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking is being repaired now so that every ad-driven contact flows through correctly; no leads are being lost, only miscounted.
